body:
> Verify that the application appropriately sanitizes untrusted input before use in Java Naming and Directory Interface (JNDI) queries and that JNDI is configured securely to prevent JNDI injection attacks.

### "sanitizes"
This creates false sense of security, because JNDI input should be validated or rejected, not stripped. JNDI is not a renderer, It’s a Name Resolver and JNDI Injection requires control over lookup strings, Not payload structure. Instead of relying on sanitization, enforce strict allowlisting of acceptable inputs like only predefined, safe JNDI names, etc.. Additionally, disable or restrict JNDI lookups to untrusted sources, Audit and update third-party libraries.
